surface_forms: ce monsieur qui a parlé dans ses vers de son « cimier de gentilhomme »

appraisal_events.evidence: « il était en tout cas de très petite souche… Jamais un vrai grand seigneur ne dit de ces choses-là… à part Cinq-Mars je n’ai jamais rien pu lire de M. de Vigny, l’ennui me fait tomber le livre des mains. M. Molé, qui avait autant d’esprit et de tact que M. de Vigny en avait peu, l’a arrangé de belle façon en le recevant à l’Académie. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Holding the floor before the deferential family, Mme de Villeparisis demolishes Vigny on grounds of birth, taste and tedium, and crowns the demolition by invoking Molé's Académie speech as a masterpiece of malice at his expense; the same caste-bound criterion is then turned on Balzac (a society « où il n’était pas reçu ») and Hugo. The narrator reports the verdicts without comment, but the criterion of social reception exposes itself, so the evaluation is staged as aristocratic reflex rather than endorsed literary judgment.

appraisal_events.evidence: « ses lumières si hostiles le premier soir, à l’arrivée, maintenant protectrices et douces, annonciatrices du foyer… le concierge, les grooms, le lift, empressés… massés sur les degrés à nous attendre, étaient devenus familiers… aidés par beaucoup plus de serviteurs qu’il n’était nécessaire, mais ils sentaient l’importance de la scène »
appraisal_events.explanation: The Balbec hotel that was hostile on the first evening is now home: the staff mass on the steps to await him, the room has become « si réellement mienne », and the narrator is reflected back to himself with affectionate fidelity. The passage explicitly and warmly narrates his passage from exclusion to belonging.

status_effects.explanation: Vigny is locally demolished on every axis Mme de Villeparisis controls: doubtful nobility, vulgar taste, unreadable works, and a public humiliation at the Académie.

She commands the floor with insider authority and remembered family testimony; the household waits to hear her and the grandmother apologizes for monopolizing her (« Nous abusons de vous »), so her local rhetorical standing rises even though the narration quietly undercuts her criteria.
The narrator is decisively included in a space that had been alien: lights turned protective, servants assembled and anxious at his lateness, a room that is now truly his own.

ambiguities: « M. Molé » is the male Académie orator (the statesman), not the reference sheet's « comtesse Molé »; the surface form is deliberately left unresolved rather than merged into that entity.

The narrator supplies no explicit comment on Mme de Villeparisis's literary verdicts within this window; the ironized reading rests on the self-exposing social criterion (« où il n’était pas reçu », « jamais un vrai grand seigneur »), so a strictly neutral-report reading remains locally available.
